skills.name: Studying living things in the field and the laboratory

note.text:
Living things can be studied in two places:
• In their natural environment (field study): we see how they really live, what they eat, where they shelter and how they behave with other living things. Tools: notebook and pencil, hand lens, collecting bags and jars, sweep net, quadrat (a square frame for counting plants), camera.
• In the laboratory: we can control the conditions, measure carefully and look closely with a microscope. But the organism is away from its real home.
The two go together: observe in the field, then study samples in the laboratory.
In the field: disturb living things as little as possible, return animals where you found them, and never collect protected species.

worked_example.problem: To learn what weaver birds use to build their nests and where they build them, should Ewane study them in the field or in the laboratory?
steps: Nest building happens in the birds’ real home, in trees near water and villages.
Watching them there shows the real behaviour.

cards.idea: A field study observes living things in their natural environment.
example: Counting the plants in a quadrat on the school field is a field study.

cards.idea: In the laboratory we control conditions and look closely, for example with a microscope.
example: Pond water is brought to the lab to look for tiny organisms.

cards.idea: In the field: disturb as little as possible, return animals and never collect protected species.
example: A frog is looked at, then put back where it was found.

check.prompt: What should you do with a frog after studying it in the field?

right.text: put it back where you found it

wrong.text: take it home as a pet
wrong.explain: Return animals to where you found them.
Put it back where it lives.

wrong.text: keep it in a jar without water

wrong.explain: Return animals to where you found them.

questions.prompt: What is an advantage of studying living things in the laboratory?

right.text: Conditions can be controlled and things looked at closely.

wrong.text: You see how the organism lives in its real home.
wrong.explain: That is an advantage of a field study.

wrong.text: The organism is always happier there.
wrong.explain: It is away from its real home.
Protected species must not be collected.

questions.prompt: One sentence is wrong. Which one?

right.text: A quadrat is used to count plants.
Field studies show how organisms really live.
A microscope is used in the laboratory.
Animals should be returned after study.

wrong.text: Protected species may be collected for fun.
wrong.explain: Protected species must never be collected.

wrong.text: In the laboratory you see an organism in its real home.
A sweep net is used to look at cells.
wrong.explain: A sweep net catches insects; a microscope shows cells.
